definition: The principle of good continuation is a Gestalt idea in which visual elements are grouped as parts of the same smooth, continuing pattern or contour. In this source, it is linked to association-field effects in early vision that support contour integration.

reasons: The definition’s explanation that good continuation is an idea where visual elements are “grouped as parts of the same smooth, continuing pattern or contour” is not explicitly stated in the provided packet text.

The packet does support that interaction maps are “similar to association fields” and “reflect the Gestalt principle of good continuation,” and that feedback signals “promote contour integration,” but it does not provide the specific “smooth, continuing pattern or contour” description included in the definition.

The general definition of the principle as grouping visual elements into a smooth, continuing pattern or contour is not stated in the packet; the packet only says the interaction maps are similar to association fields and reflect the Gestalt principle of good continuation.

The definition slightly overstates the source by presenting a general Gestalt account as if it were defined in the article, rather than limiting itself to the article’s specific link between association fields, good continuation, and contour integration in early vision.
